messages.subject: Re: Show images in shiny using an id from a single dataframe
parts:
I don't know how your countrydata.csv looks like and if you want to use the ID column? In that case you should use data$ID instead of just ID
Be aware that R is case sensitive so Data is not the same as data!

Below a simple working example

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

#data = read.csv("countrydata.csv") 
data <- data.frame(State = c("AB", "AB", "CD", "CD"), City = c("A", "B", "C", "D"), out = c(1, 2, 3, 4), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- fluidPage(

# Application title
  titlePanel("Test"),
  
  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins 
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("State", "State",
choices = c("Enter a State", data$State))

),
    
    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(

plotOutput("plot")
    )
  )

)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output)

{
  c_id <- reactive({
    shiny::validate(
      shiny::need(input$State, "Select a State!")
    )

data[data$State == input$State, ]
  })
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    req(input$State != "Enter a State")
    ggplot(data = c_id()) + geom_bar(aes(x = City, y = out), stat="identity") + ggtitle(paste("State:", input$State))

})
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

On Tuesday, May 23, 2017 at 1:16:53 PM UTC+5:30, g inberg wrote:
I don't know how your countrydata.csv looks like and if you want to use the ID column? In that case you should use data$ID instead of just ID
Be aware that R is case sensitive so Data is not the same as data!

Below a simple working example

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

#data = read.csv("countrydata.csv") 
data <- data.frame(State = c("AB", "AB", "CD", "CD"), City = c("A", "B", "C", "D"), out = c(1, 2, 3, 4), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
ui <- fluidPage(

  # Application title
  titlePanel("Test"),
  
  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins 
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("State", "State",
                  choices = c("Enter a State", data$State))
    ),
    
    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("plot")
    )
  )
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
server <- function(input, output)
{
  c_id <- reactive({
    shiny::validate(
      shiny::need(input$State, "Select a State!")
    )
    data[data$State == input$State, ]
  })
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    req(input$State != "Enter a State")
    ggplot(data = c_id()) + geom_bar(aes(x = City, y = out), stat="identity") + ggtitle(paste("State:", input$State))
  })
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
